body:
## Problem

PR #670 (#652) makes "not clean" spread along `Depends on` edges among the finished ids the pre-wave carry judges, but only for "not clean" judged **before** the fold (from PR state and head). The brief set the fold-time case aside as a known residual (`results/issue_652/brief.md:43`, finding 1). The sign-off accepted that limit (§6, citing `docs/07-crosscutting.md:696` and `flow.py:920` on #670's branch). No issue tracks it.

The case: `integrate.fold` with `skipped=` records a merge failure for one bundle and goes on to the next (`integrate.py:433-439`). The carry adds that id to `why` only **after** the fold. Take a finished P that is clean by state but conflicts at fold time, followed in the same fold by a finished Q with `Depends on: P` whose branch contains P. Q is folded, so P's commits reach the line through Q's branch, even though P itself was skipped. That breaks the carry's invariant: never put work onto the line that the run judged not clean, directly or through another finished bundle's branch.

The issue_652 reviewer reproduced it independently ("an independently exercised fold-time conflict still carries the dependent and prerequisite ancestry", `results/issue_652/brief.md:46`).

## Done when

A finished P skipped at fold time keeps every finished dependent whose branch contains P off the line. Either prune dependents during the fold, or re-fold without them. The dependents are held and named with P as the cause. A real-git test pins P (fold conflict) → Q (finished, `Depends on: P`, branch cut from P): after the carry, the line has none of P's commits.

Relates to #652, #624, #653. Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-10 (issue_652).
title: stack mode: a prerequisite skipped at fold time still reaches the line through a finished dependent's branch (#652 residual)
